items.title: Billy Bauer interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, March 22, 1998
items.q: like Max, when I played with him, I used to sit behind, down on 52nd Street

ctx.x: That’s right. And that’s what does it after a while. Well Davy was, he was like, it’s hard to say because he wasn’t a drummer that was a flashy drummer, you know or something. But he’d get into a certain place and he would just stay there, you couldn’t get him away from that, and the band would eventually get with him. With Max, I say that in the book too, like Max, when I played with him, I used to sit behind, down on 52nd Street, Charlie’s band was out there and then I was in the back with the other band that,…
It felt like he was speeding up kind of, or just the intensity?
